w: Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha at the Shree Swaminarayan Mandir in Bhayandar and sanctified the under construction mandir on Mira road.

Swamishri conveyed his New Year's Jai Swaminarayan to all sadhus and devotees. Prior to his morning puja, Swamishri did darshan and offered his respects at Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj's rooms and in Akshar Deri. Therafter he performed the murti pratishtha rituals of murtis to be installed in a new mandir in Madankundla village. ( The murtis were consecrated by senior sadhus in the newly built Swaminarayan Mandir in Madankundla on 20 November 2001.)

In the New Year's morning assembly at 11.45 am Swamishri blessed the congregation, " ... Gunatitanand Swami has said, 'What we need we have get so do not think you are miserable.' We have the association of God and his holy sadhu, hence there is no higher happiness than this ... When one believes oneself as atma then there will be no misery. Today, on New Year's Day, pray to God to bless oneself with happiness, that is, one's 'dehbhav' be erased and be able to eternally remember God. When one attains this, then one shall become happy ..."

The evening assembly was dedicated as Youth Day and the diksha of Swamishri by Shastriji Maharaj. Two dramas about Akshar Deri were performed. Shri Haka Khachar narrated the history of Akshar Mandir. This was followed by a folk dance by youths and Pujya Viveksagar Swami recalled incidents of Yogiji Maharaj. Finally Swamishri blessed the congregation.

In the morning a special Tribal Assembly was held. From early morning tribal devotees from scores of tribal villages in the Sabarkantha region arrived in dozens of trucks. Over 4300 devotees were present for this special tribal assembly. Following speeches by senior sadhus, stories about tribal devotees whose wayward lives had been transformed through satsang were narrated and they were blessed by Swamishri. To mark this special occasion tribal youths performed exiting traditional dances in the presence of Swamishri. Finally, Swamishri blessed the assembly.
At 9.25 a.m. Swamishri reached Sirohi and a ddressed the devotees and well-wishers in Hindi.
At 10.00 a.m. Swamishri visited Sumerpur and blessed the devotees and well-wishers.

At 11.45 a.m. Swamishri arrived in Pali. Swamishri blessed Pruthvisinh Bapu, an aged devotee. At 6.30 p.m. Swamishri attended a public satsang assembly. Prior to Swamishri's blessings, Shri Harikrishna Maharaj was honored.

A teenager had come to Pramukh Swami Maharaj in the meeting room. As is natural at his age, the influence of the local environment had grown in the life of this London teenager. Swamishri lovingly turned him back and asked, "What about meat?"
"I take it now and then."

Speaking to the teenager with feeling, Swamishri said, "It is man's dharma to try to see that other living beings live. Only such a person can be called human. Only if we live that way can life be called a success. Otherwise, if we kill others and eat them, how can that be called humanity? How would we feel if someone killed one of our loved ones and ate them? Just as we feel pain, animals also have a soul. They too love their young. See how lovingly a cow licks her calf! If we kill such animals and birds, what humanity is there in that? It is a sin. So today, since you have come to God, do this much. Alcohol, meat and cigarettes are useless. Give them all up."
Moved by Swamishri's heartfelt, loving words, the teenager said, "Swami, from today I give it all up."
Swamishri's Ganga of love has effortlessly turned many such youths who had lost their way onto the true path of life.

BAPS volunteers presented a short discussion on the principles of Akshar-Purushottam and the efforts of Shastriji Maharaj. Swamishri was very pleased and inspired them, “We have to repeat the same thing again and again, that is, (the philosophy of) Akshar and Purushottam. Like we eat dal, vegetables and rice daily (we should repeat the same knowledge of Akshar and Purushottam).” Swamishri then asked a devotee seated before him, “What do you do when you get to the office? You have to answer phone calls!” The devotee replied in affirmation. “Then what do you do the next day?” Swamishri enquired. “The same thing,” the devotee answered. “Then it is the same for spiritual matters. Like you never get fed up of attending to telephone calls, you should never get bored in doing this repeatedly. This is what you have to do.” Swamishri inspired the volunteers to understand and consolidate their understanding of the core principles of satsang.

To please Bhagwan Swaminarayan and guru Pramukh Swami Maharaj children, youths and senior devotees perform austerities, pilgrimages and other devotional means. The spiritual endeavours performed by devotees during Swamishri’s visit to the local centres are congratulatory and worthy of recognition. They also reflect Swamishri’s divinity for inspiring such spiritual efforts in children, teenagers and devotees.
Eight devotees pilgrimaged by foot from Paddhari–Moviya. Eight youths cycled from Sankari (450 km).

A welcome assembly was held in the evening. A traditional Swagatam dance was performed by children. After speeches and bhajans by BAPS youths, Swamishri was garlanded by senior sadhus. In conclusion, Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Yogiji Maharaj daily prayed in the Akshar Deri for Satsang, sadhus and mandirs to increase manifold. At that time it seemed that Yogi Maharaj was merely uttering words. But today we see, through his grace, the immense growth of Satsang. The aim of our birth is to become akshar-rup and worship Purushottam. You may do your daily work but you must have one aim. It’s like a businessman who has one target – how to earn more! Those who study at college have the aim of acquiring a degree. One should perform such works in life that God becomes immensely pleased. By doing good work in the day one gets sound sleep…” More than 18,000 devotees attended the satsang assembly.

ds.t: So you need not stretch out your hand
w: A middle aged devotee phoned from London. He wished to send a financial donation to the mandir. After hearing him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj first asked about his financial situation and then said, "Your seva is already there. You may need it in the future, so it is fine if you do not do it now."

The middle aged devotee explained his situation in detail, yet Swamishri said, "There is provision, so there is no problem, but if you have something with you, you will not have to stretch out your hand to anyone. So if it is convenient, do a little seva, so that you have peace within."

A middle-aged devotee phoned from London. He wished to send a financial offering to the mandir. After listening to him, Pramukh Swami Maharaj first asked about his financial situation and then said, "Your seva is already counted. You may need it in the future, so it does not matter if you do not give now."

The middle-aged devotee explained his situation in detail, yet Swamishri said, "There are arrangements in place, so it does not matter. But if you have something of your own, you will not have to stretch out your hand to anyone. So if it is convenient, do a little seva, so that you feel peace within."

This morning, while Mahant Swami Maharaj was absorbed in his letter work, the sadhus organising the children's shibir asked him, "Yesterday, when you were moving the anjan shalaka (the golden rod used to consecrate murtis) before all the volunteers, what were you saying?"
"May everyone be well." Saying this, Swamishri naturally added, "I keep saying this all the time, the whole day. May everyone be well."
"In his heart there is not, even by mistake, any bad thought of hurting anyone; every moment, from within, arises the wish to do good to others..."
This way of the true Sant is ever present in Swamishri.

Today, when Mahant Swami Maharaj came out of his room, a devotee was introduced: "This is the grandson of Shamji Ada, his daughter's son." His name was Harsh. On account of him, remembering Shashank, the son of his maternal aunt, Swamishri said, "A caesarean was to be done for him, but after we prayed, it went well."
The amazing thing was that in 1987 Shamjibhai had told Swamishri and prayed. As a result Shashank was born without a caesarean or any complication.
The prayer made 30 years ago for a child came to Swamishri's mind as soon as he saw that child's cousin! Did it come to mind, or did he always remember it?!

Speaking of a dignitary who came to today's meetings, Rohitbhai Patel (Paper Mill), Abhayswarupdas Swami said, "He is a man of very firm will and strong, but he passed by after receiving Mahant Swami Maharaj's blessings and real tears came to his eyes, and he said, 'What radiance there is in his eyes!' It seemed as if he had melted."
Today, giving his blessings in the evening assembly, Mahant Swami Maharaj showered these words:

"We are not ordinary. Shriji Maharaj said, 'Countless kalpas have passed...' One kalpa means 8 billion 640 million years. If we take ten million of those and put the other 8 billion 630 million years in a fixed deposit, then in that ten million, two Satyugs, two Tretas, two Dwapars and two Kaliyugs pass. If in just ten million there are two each of Satyug and the others, then in 8 billion 640 million years, ages upon ages pass.

Maharaj said, 'Not one kalpa but countless kalpas have passed, but if in them one had found satsang, birth and death would not have remained.' For how many ages, for how long have we been going round in this cycle?! Then Shriji Maharaj said another thing: 'When does a human body come? After going round 8.4 million births, a human body comes once. In those 8.4 million rounds, as many years pass as a seven followed by 25 zeros, and then one human body comes.'
Then he said: a human body does come, but it may come anywhere, there is no certainty. Then the human life passes just like that of an animal. There is no awareness at all of 'Why have we been born?'
Then Maharaj said: a human body does come, but birth in a noble family comes in the land of India, nowhere else. See from where to where we have come!
Then Maharaj said, 'After getting birth in a noble family, one may attain the realm of the gods and the realm of Brahma, but contact with the manifest form of God is extremely rare.'

Where we are sitting! We have attained great persons like Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Yogibapa and Shastriji Maharaj. Lust, anger and greed will all go away like this (snapping his fingers). Maharaj said: once this form is recognised, then just as mahuda flowers drop pit pat, lust and anger fall away.
See, we have attained Pramukh Swami Maharaj, we have attained Yogibapa, we have attained Shastriji Maharaj, what a great thing has happened! Our work is done."
